threads.body:
The parent lookup, and with it the whole `_InvocationState.conversation_id` plumbing, looks redundant: LangChain merges a run's config metadata into every descendant run, so a nested callback already receives `thread_id`/`session_id`/`conversation_id` in its own `metadata`.

Checked with langchain-core 1.6.1 / langgraph 1.x: an id set once via `with_config({"metadata": ...})` or via `configurable.thread_id` reaches the metadata of every chain, chat and tool callback below it, including a model call made inside a tool body that never forwards the config:

```
tool ask   {'thread_id': 't1'}   parent=False
chat       {'thread_id': 't1'}   parent=True
```

If there is a case where metadata does not propagate, a test that fails without the inheritance would pin it down. Otherwise resolving from `metadata` alone drops the extra `add_invocation_state` parameter, the `_InvocationState` field and `get_conversation_id`.

         if not invocation.span.is_recording():
             self._invocation_manager.delete_invocation_state(run_id=run_id)
 
+    def _resolve_conversation_id(
+        self, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None, parent_run_id: UUID | None
+    ) -> str | None:
+        if metadata:
+            for key in CONVERSATION_ID_METADATA_KEYS:
+                conversation_id = metadata.get(key)
+                if conversation_id:
+                    return str(conversation_id)
+
+        # The application attaches the id to a single point in the chain, so a
+        # run without one of its own tries to inherit from its nearest ancestor.
+        return self._invocation_manager.get_conversation_id(parent_run_id)

Thanks for calling it out, I checked and it turns out what you said is correct! 
I've removed the parent lookup, also removed the field from `_InvocationState`, now `conversation.id` comes from metadata only. Sorry for the confusion.
